mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a >0.5% decrease in FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP by more than 2% year-over-year indicates strong economic growth, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 returns higher over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a >2% YoY increase in GDPC1 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a >0.5% decrease in UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% month-over-month signals increased economic activity, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 returns higher over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a >1% MoM increase in INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over the past two months indicates a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to increased demand for related goods and services, driving S&P 500 returns higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 do not show a significant positive correlation with the trend in HOUST (correlation coefficient p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and CPI is increasing by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure and potential tightening by the Fed, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following the specified trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3% in the past month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following the specified trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is positive and housing starts are increasing, it signals a robust demand environment, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 returns higher over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 positive growth and HOUST increase
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following the specified trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).
